guard: the deployer instrument mints on the legacy rail: it is the one unbounded instrument, and an issuance with no lifecycle gate must carry an expiry, so folding it into the issuance arm refuses every cotal down at mint
why: The CLI's instruments mint through connectOrThrow. The control-caller tiers are five-minute
one-shots, so their issuance evidence carries the credential's own expiry as its liveness. The
deployer has no default TTL (a deploy spans launches and readiness waits), and the mint refuses
an issuance that has neither a source gate nor an expiry. Measured live: `cotal down` printed
the mint refusal and exited non-zero on every static mesh. The mutation puts the deployer back
on the issuance arm; the cell that mints it through the shipped path is the one that reddens.

mutations.name: the deployer is minted as an issuance again
mutations.expectRed: deployer mints through the shipped connect path
mutations.note: A bare `if (false)` narrows `role` and the branch no longer typechecks, so the suite never runs. The comparison against a pin no command passes keeps the types and sends the deployer down the issuance arm.
